# Automate the balance-tuning loop: baseline, single-edit, re-run and diff

> **Headline:** Add a `--tune` mode to the batch-evaluation CLI that runs a
> baseline batch, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs the *identical*
> sweep and writes a versioned before/after comparison with per-metric deltas
> and a readable summary — so a tuning attempt becomes one auditable,
> repeatable command instead of a manual chore.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature · **Discovered from:** <<AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW>>

## Problem statement

The automated-balancing framework (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) provides the *evidence*
(batch reports with distribution statistics) but the *loop* around it is still
manual and error-prone. A designer who wants to tune a knob must, by hand:
(1) run a baseline batch, (2) edit a CSV, (3) re-run the identical command,
(4) diff the JSON/text reports and interpret per-metric deltas across a table
of distributions. Human error creeps in exactly where the tool exists to remove
it: forgetting to keep seeds identical, comparing reports from different batch
configs, or misreading which metrics actually moved. The acceptance-verification
run already had to do this diff by hand (see docs/BALANCING.md §Acceptance-verification run).

There is no automation that: records a baseline, applies a single proposed edit
(guided), re-runs against the *same* seeds/config, and produces a per-metric
before/after comparison with guidance on whether each delta looks like the
intended effect.

## Users

- **As a game designer / maintainer**, I want to run one command that (baseline → edit → re-run → compare) reports exactly which balance metrics moved and by how much, so tuning becomes a fast, auditable loop instead of a manual chore.
- **As a producer**, I want a durable, repeatable record of each tuning attempt (edit, config snapshot, before/after reports) so balance history can be reviewed and reverted.

## Expected behaviour

- A `--tune` mode on the existing `scripts/evaluate.mjs` entry point (Q1-b)
  that:
  1. Runs the baseline batch (identical seeds/config/policy) and captures the report.
  2. Applies a single, **declarative** CSV edit supplied by the caller
     (e.g. `--set enemy-configs.csv boss.health=6`) — Q2-a; the tool can
     **restore** the original file on completion so the checkout stays clean.
  3. Re-runs the identical batch and emits a **before/after comparison**
     artifact (per-metric deltas: mean/median/stdDev per distribution, plus
     per-archetype kill and per-upgrade deltas) alongside both full reports.
  4. Prints a human-readable summary identifying the metrics that moved beyond
     a **relative ±10% default threshold** on mean/median (configurable via
     `--threshold`) — Q3-a — and flags distribution-shape changes (e.g. stdDev
     growth = variance increase, median shifts).
- No production runtime impact; all new logic stays in the dev/eval layer
  (`src/ai/eval/`, Node shell). Determinism guarantees are preserved
  byte-for-byte.

## Suggested approach

- Reuse the existing irreproducibility guard: the comparison must verify both batches used identical sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) before reporting deltas — an empty diff check confirms no side effects.
- Pure diff/aggregation logic in the TS core (`src/ai/eval/`) with a thin shell wrapper in `scripts/evaluate.mjs`; no wall-clock or I/O in the pure core (same constraint as the epic).
- Where CSV edit support lands, reuse the shared loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` via `hydrateBalanceConfig` from `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts`) so the re-run reads the edited values.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1: One-command loop.** A documented `--tune` command runs baseline, applies one declarative CSV edit, re-runs with an identical sweep, and writes three artifacts: baseline report, candidate report, and a versioned before/after comparison (per-metric count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev deltas, per-archetype and per-upgrade deltas).
- **AC2: Same-sweep guard.** The tool refuses to compare batches whose sweep configuration (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) differs, and errors on a non-empty byte-diff of identical-config re-runs (detects side effects).
- **AC3: Deterministic comparison.** Same edit + same seeds yields a byte-identical comparison artifact; independently-derived (empty) deltas are zero.
- **AC4: Safe restore.** After the run the CSV is byte-identical to its pre-run state on success **and** failure paths (or the user opted into keeping the edit), verified by test; the working tree is clean unless the user says otherwise.
- **AC5: Readable summary.** The text output flags metrics that moved beyond a configurable threshold (relative ±10% mean/median default) and notes distribution-shape changes (stdDev/median shifts), with the same statistics echoed in the machine-readable artifact.
- **AC6: Tests.** Pure comparison/aggregation, the same-sweep guard, safe restore and determinism are covered by unit tests; no wall-clock/IO leaks into the pure core.
- **AC7: Documentation.** `docs/BALANCING.md` gains a `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section with the worked example; README references it.
- **AC8: Full project test suite passes** with the new changes.
- **AC9: All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (e.g. `docs/EVALUATION.md` if the CLI flags there are extended).

## Constraints

- **Determinism (preserve AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 AC5).** Every run derives from a seed; no wall clock; the before/after comparison is reproducible byte-for-byte for the same edit + seeds.
- **Dev/eval only.** No production runtime impact; `src/ai/eval/` stays pure (no I/O, no wall clock); filesystem work (CSV edit/restore, artifact writes) stays in the Node shell (`scripts/evaluate.mjs`).
- **Single source of truth.** The re-run reads the edited values through the shared config loaders (`src/core/configStore.ts` / `hydrateBalanceConfig`), never a divergent copy.
- **Gym↔game parity.** Any shared gameplay behaviour exercised by the tune loop must come from the shared core; the tune loop is a dev tool like the gyms.
- **No PII.** Reuse the existing telemetry schema and redaction policy.
- **Bounded resources.** Two batches (baseline + candidate) must not exhaust memory; reuse the batch runner's incremental aggregation.
- **Checkout hygiene.** The CSV restore must leave the working tree clean on success **and** failure unless the user opts in to keeping the edit (AC4).

## Existing state

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — thin Node shell (Vite SSR module loader, file I/O); already parses `--batch`, `--games`, `--policies`, `--seed(s)`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`, `--json`; writes `balance-report.json`, `balance-report.txt`, `runs.jsonl` under `--out` (default `eval-output/`, git-ignored).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` — `runBatch` sweeps seeds × policies deterministically; the batch config (seeds, policies, ticks, dt, sampleEveryTicks) is recorded in `BatchOutput.json`.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceStats.ts`-family extraction (`metrics.ts`) and aggregation; `BALANCE_STATISTICS_SCHEMA_VERSION`-versioned `BalanceRunStats` / `BalanceAggregate` (`src/ai/eval/types.ts`) with `DistributionStats` (count/mean/median/min/max/stdDev), per-archetype `enemiesKilledByArchetype` and per-upgrade `upgradesSelected`.
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — stable serialisation + human-readable summary.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — `hydrateBalanceConfig()` loads the real `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `ship-config.csv`, `difficulty-curves.csv`; `ENEMY_CSV_PATH` etc. exported.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — documents the batch runner; its §Acceptance-verification run shows the (manual) CSV-edit diff that this item automates.
- The batch report already hashes the config and records seeds, so the same-sweep guard's inputs exist today.

## Desired change

1. Extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode (Q1-b) that chains baseline → single declarative edit → re-run → compare in one command.
2. Add declarative CSV-edit support (`--set <file>.<field>=<value>`, Q2-a) with guaranteed restore (AC4).
3. Add pure diff/aggregation logic in `src/ai/eval/` producing a versioned before/after comparison artifact (per-metric deltas, per-archetype/per-upgrade deltas).
4. Emit a human-readable summary flagging metrics moved beyond the configurable ±10% relative threshold and noting shape changes (stdDev/median) (AC5).
5. Enforce the same-sweep guard (AC2) and determinism (AC3).
6. Document the tuning loop in `docs/BALANCING.md` with the worked example; reference from README (AC7).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` — new `--tune` mode: orchestrate baseline/edit/re-run/compare, CSV edit + restore, artifact writes (shell layer only).
- `src/ai/eval/engine.ts` or new `src/ai/eval/tune.ts` — pure tuning-loop core: same-sweep guard, before/after comparison + aggregation, determinism.
- `src/ai/eval/types.ts` — versioned before/after comparison types (deltas per metric/archetype/upgrade).
- `src/ai/eval/report.ts` — comparison rendering (readable summary + stable JSON).
- `src/util/csvEdit.ts` (new, shell-adjacent) — declarative single-field CSV edit with restore; or handled inside the `.mjs` shell.
- `src/ai/eval/balanceConfig.ts` / `src/core/configStore.ts` — reused via `hydrateBalanceConfig` so the re-run reads edited values.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — new `Tuning loop (baseline → edit → re-run → compare)` section; README reference.
- Tests: new unit tests alongside `src/ai/eval/engine.test.ts` / `report.test.ts`; CLI shell tests next to `scripts/evaluate-args.test.ts`.

## Related work

- **Epic: Automated Balancing** (AH-0MV1DLUZ8009OCJW) — completed; this item closes the loop around it.
- **Extend the headless arena to the full campaign** (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) — open; once landed, per-wave/per-upgrade fields in the schema become populated and the tune loop's per-upgrade deltas become fully meaningful; not blocking this item (the loop diffs whatever the arena reports).
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — in progress; the tune loop and the validation share the same versioned balance-statistics schema and will interoperate (tune → re-baseline → validate).
- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — completed; shared schema consumer.

(Also see the automated related-work report appended to the item description.)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: CSV edit corrupts the checkout.** Mitigated by AC4 (restore on success and failure paths, tested; explicit opt-out to keep the edit).
- **Risk: comparing incompatible batches produces misleading deltas.** Mitigated by AC2 same-sweep guard (refuse on differing seeds/policies/ticks/dt/sampleEveryTicks) plus the empty byte-diff side-effect check.
- **Risk: "the intended effect" is subjective.** The tool reports and flags, it does not assert intent; the threshold default (±10% relative on mean/median) is configurable and documented.
- **Risk: scope creep** (interactive edit prompt, multi-edit batches, auto-apply best candidate, wave/upgrade tuning once the campaign arena lands). Recorded as follow-up opportunities, not in scope here.
- **Assumption: the current arena output is sufficient** for a useful first tuning loop (wave/upgrade fields may still be unpopulated until AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A; per-archetype and minerals/survival deltas are already meaningful).
- **Assumption: `--tune` reuses the existing batch flags** (`--games`, `--policies`, `--seeds`, `--ticks`, `--dt`, `--sample-every`, `--out`) with no new sweep semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Entry point — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode, or add a new peer `scripts/balance-tune.mjs`? **Recommended:** peer script (clearer separation)." — Answer (operator): "b" — extend `scripts/evaluate.mjs` with a `--tune` mode. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q2: "Edit interface for v1 — declarative `--set` only, or also an interactive prompt? **Recommended:** declarative `--set` only (deterministic, scriptable, testable without a TTY)." — Answer (operator): "a" — declarative `--set` only for v1; interactive prompt deferred. Source: interactive reply, this session.
- Q3: "'Moved significantly' default threshold — relative ±10% of baseline mean/median, absolute per-metric defaults, or relative + stdDev growth flag? **Recommended:** relative ±10% (scale-free across metrics)." — Answer (operator): "a" — relative ±10% default on mean/median, configurable via `--threshold`; stdDev/median shape-flagging retained per AC5. Source: interactive reply, this session.

# Intake Brief — Mystery UFO visible collector drone

## Problem statement

The `mystery_ufo` power-up exists only as an **invisible instant mineral + score
bounty** routed through the effects registry — there is no actual UFO entity on
screen. This work makes the Mystery UFO visibly real: the player ship spawns a
small collector drone (a scaled copy of the player ship) that actively seeks and
collects minerals, then flies back and pays out, with an upgrade path and a
full-hull permanent auto-spawn.

## Users

- **As a player**, I want to *see* the Mystery UFO I earned — a little ship that
  cruises the arena, hoovers up minerals and brings them home — so the reward is
  tangible instead of an invisible bank-credit.
- **As a game designer**, I want the drone's performance (lifetime, capacity,
  collector radius, spawn interval) to scale with the power-up level on the
  shared curve, so it grows with the run without re-tuning code.
- **As a developer**, I want the drone behaviour to live in the shared core and
  be exercised identically by the game and `GymPowerUpsUtility`, so the
  gym↔game parity rule (AGENTS.md, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) holds.

### Example user stories

- As a player, when I collect a `mystery_ufo` drop I see a small copy of my ship
  spawn, collect up to 10 minerals (more at higher levels), fly back within ~5 s,
  and pay out the minerals into my hold.
- As a player, once I permanently apply `mystery_ufo` from a full hull, my ship
  re-spawns the drone every 30 s (faster at higher levels) for the rest of the run.
- As a player, if an enemy bullet or an enemy hits the drone, it is destroyed and
  drops its held minerals **plus** a `2 × level` mineral bonus where it fell.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `mystery_ufo` field pickup no longer grants an instant mineral/score burst:
  it spawns exactly one visible collector drone (a scaled-down player-ship
  entity, code-drawn neon-vector, no external art). Verified by a unit test that
  the spawn request produces a drone entity and does **not** queue a direct
  `_mysteryBonus` payout.
- The drone actively seeks the nearest live mineral, collects minerals whose
  centre enters its collector radius, returns to the player and pays out when it
  has collected its capacity **or** its lifetime expires (whichever comes first),
  and disappears after payout. Level-0 defaults: lifetime 5 s, capacity 10
  minerals, collector radius 20 px. Verified by shared-core tests asserting the
  seek → collect → return → pay out flow and the lifetime/capacity
  termination, with the exact pay-in-minerals semantics.
- The drone's lifetime, capacity, collector radius and (permanent) spawn interval
  resolve from `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` on the shared curve per the agreed defaults
  (lifetime 5→8 s, capacity 10→20, radius 20→40 px, spawn interval 30→12 s,
  `k=0.3`), verified by a monotonic level-resolution test; the retired
  `mysteryUfoScore` level variable is removed from specs (or repurposed) and its
  tests updated.
- The full-hull (permanent) reward enables a timer that spawns a drone every
  30 s at Lvl 0, decreasing per level to the agreed cap; a field-pickup
  (non-permanent) collection spawns exactly one drone. Verified by a test using
  a mock clock/stepping update that the permanent timer fires at the resolved
  interval and the non-permanent path spawns a single drone per pickup.
- An enemy bullet or enemy body collision destroys the drone; the player's own
  fire cannot. On destruction the drone drops its held minerals plus a
  `2 × level` mineral bonus at its position (minerals land as collectable field
  deposits). Verified by a shared-core test covering enemy-bullet hit, enemy
  collision and player-bullet pass-through.
- The drone behaviour is implemented once in the shared core and consumed by
  `PlayScene` and `GymPowerUpsUtility` (threat-free utility power-up gym);
  `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` stays green and the gym parity docs
  assertion holds. A gym test observes the drone spawn/collect/return lifecycle.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` §8, the GDD power-up
  catalogue, README and any relevant help/HUD copy.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Neon-vector aesthetic, code-drawn graphics only** (GDD §7.2) — the drone is a
  code-drawn scaled copy of the player ship; no external art assets.
- **Gym↔game parity** — the drone entity and its lifecycle live in the shared
  core (`src/scenes/core/`), consumed by the game and `GymPowerUpsUtility`;
  enforced by `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the parity
  docs assertion. A gym that must diverge requires a recorded reason.
- **Tuning is data, not code** — all per-level values resolve through
  `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` on the single shared curve (`src/utils/curve.ts`).
- **Existing seams reused** — the drone is a new entity in the shared core
  following the existing seek-steering pattern (`setSeekTargets`, e.g. the
  Harvester seeker), not a new per-scene copy; the drop pipeline and mineral
  layer are shared already.
- **No enemy–enemy collisions** (GDD §2.6) applies to the drone as a friendly
  entity; its only collisions are enemy bullets/enemy bodies.
- **Retire cleanly** — the instant `mysteryUfoScore`/`mysteryUfoMinerals`
  burst path and its HUD "timed window" semantics are removed or repurposed
  without leaving dead registry paths (dead code may be mentioned, not left
  dangling).

## Existing state

- `mystery_ufo` is a catalogue `PowerUpId` (AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7, shipped
  v0.1.11): an instant mineral+score burst queued via `EffectsRegistry`
  (`src/powerups/effects.ts` → `consumeMysteryBonus`) and drained by
  `CombatCoreScene` (`bonus.minerals` → hold, `bonus.score` → run total).
- Level variables `mysteryUfoMinerals` (base 2→cap 6) and `mysteryUfoScore`
  (base 250→cap 1500) in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`; drop weight 3 in
  `src/core/rules.ts`; code-drawn saucer icon in `src/powerups/icons.ts`; HUD
  row with no timed window (`src/ui/HUD.ts`, permanent-show while level > 0).
- The shared combat core already hands the live mineral field to seeking
  entities (`enemyTargeting.ts` `pushSeekTargets` + `setSeekTargets`), and the
  `Harvester` enemy already seeks minerals — a ready-made pattern for the drone.
- The full-hull permanent reward path exists (`applyCollect(id, permanent=true)`
  from the hold-full choice) and `mineralLayer` already owns the collectable
  mineral deposits the drone will ferry.

## Desired change

Replace the invisible instant bounty with a real collector-drone entity:

1. **Spawn** — field pickup spawns one drone; permanent (full-hull) reward arms a
   periodic spawn (30 s @ Lvl 0, decreasing per level to the agreed cap).
2. **Behaviour** — drone seeks nearest mineral, vacuums those within its collector
   radius (20 px @ Lvl 0), returns to the player and pays minerals into the hold
   when full or when its lifetime expires (5 s @ Lvl 0).
3. **Upgrades** — lifetime, capacity, collector radius, spawn interval grow on
   the shared curve; `mysteryUfoScore` retired or repurposed.
4. **Destruction** — enemy bullet or enemy body destroys it; it drops held
   minerals + `2 × level` mineral bonus at the crash site; player fire passes
   through.
5. **Parity** — entity lives in shared core; `PlayScene` + `GymPowerUpsUtility`
   consume it; equivalence + gym tests stay green.

## Key Files:

- `src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` — **New.** Collector-drone entity (scaled
  player-ship minimap): seek-steering via `setSeekTargets`, collector-radius
  vacuum, return/payout, lifetime/capacity termination, destruction-drop rule.
- `src/scenes/core/combatDrone.ts` (or similar shared helper) — **New.**
  Shared spawn/tick/teardown pass over the drone, mirroring `dropLayer.ts` /
  `mineralLayer.ts` style; pay-in minerals sink reuse.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — **Updated.** Spawn the drone on
  `mystery_ufo` collection (field vs permanent), feed the live mineral field to
  the drone each tick, drain earned minerals into the hold, handle destruction
  drops; remove/repurpose `consumeMysteryBonus`.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — **Updated.** Order the drone pass with the
  other shared stages; enemy-bullet/body-vs-drone collision checks.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — **Updated.** `mystery_ufo` collection queues a
  spawn request (field: one; permanent: arm timer) instead of the instant bounty;
  retire `_mysteryBonus`/`consumeMysteryBonus` or repurpose.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — **Updated.** New variable
  `mysteryUfoLifetime` (5→8 s), `mysteryUfoCapacity` (10→20), `mysteryUfoRadius`
  (20→40 px), `mysteryUfoSpawnInterval` (30→12 s), `k=0.3`; remove
  `mysteryUfoScore` (and repoint `mysteryUfoMinerals` if no longer used by the
  instant path).
- `src/scenes/core/enemyTargeting.ts` — **Updated.** Include the drone in
  `pushSeekTargets` seekers.
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — **Updated/verified.** Drone state row (level-driven) reflects
  the new semantics; no timed-window row.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts` — **Verified/exercised.** Existing saucer icon stays as
  the drop's icon.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` (+ test) — **Updated.** Exercise the
  drone spawn/seek/collect/return lifecycle threat-free; destruction covered by
  shared-core tests.
- `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` §8, GDD §4.4, README — **Updated.**
  Document the visible drone adaptation and the retired score burst.

## Related work

- **Space Invaders mystery UFO bonus (AH-0MV1BIXFO006Z1I7)** — completed,
  shipped v0.1.11; the instant-bounty implementation this item replaces. This
  item's ACs are not satisfied by the shipped work (no visible entity), so it is
  a partial-overlap rewrite, linked above.
- **New power-ups and weapons from classic arcade games (AH-0MV14SO0G0095IJ4)** —
  completed epic; §8 of `docs/CLASSIC_POWERUP_WEAPON_RESEARCH.md` is the design
  source for `mystery_ufo`.
- **Mineral scoop attraction helper + wiring (AH-0MUTPEJNO002V2NA,
  AH-0MUTPEJZL008LGDP)** — completed; the shared mineral attraction pattern the
  drone's collector radius can mirror.
- **Harvester enemy (mineral seeker)** — the existing entity whose
  seek-steering (`setSeekTargets` + `enemyTargeting.pushSeekTargets`) is the
  drone's pattern precedent.
- **Hold-full permanent reward path (AH-0MUV5CLVO002ZHS9)** — completed; the
  `applyCollect(id, permanent)` channel the drone's auto-spawn timer hooks.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Balance risk** — a periodic free collector could accelerate the economy.
  Mitigation: rare drop weight (currently 3), capped per-level growth, and the
  max-fields are modest by design; tune in data, not code.
- **Behaviour-change risk** — replacing the instant burst changes existing
  recorded behaviour shipped in v0.1.11 (tests, HUD semantics, bot content
  `src/ai/framework/competent/content.ts` and `powerUpWeights` docs). Mitigation:
  update the shipped tests/docs in the same change; the smart-capture content
  value stays valid for a passive reward.
- **Complexity risk** — a new shared entity with seek/payout/destruction paths
  could leak into per-scene code. Mitigation: single shared helper + gym parity
  tests; the seeker precedent narrows the surface.
- **Scope-creep risk** — drone skins, enemy behaviour on drones, or extra
  reward mechanics are out of scope; record them as linked work items, not scope.
- **Assumption** — "level 0" in the description means the `mystery_ufo`
  power-up's initial level; growth is monotonic per the agreed defaults.
- **Assumption** — the drone counts as a friendly entity: it cannot be harmed by
  player fire, does not collide with enemies except via the destruction rule, and
  its returned minerals enter the ship's hold like any collected mineral.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "How does the collector drone get created and what is its relationship to
  the existing `mystery_ufo` power-up?" — Answer (operator): **(A) Replace** —
  a field pickup spawns exactly one drone (no direct instant burst); the
  full-hull permanent reward adds a periodic auto-spawn (30 s @ Lvl 0,
  decreasing per level). Source: interactive reply.
- Q2 "How does the drone move and collect?" — Answer (operator): **(B) Active
  seeker** — flies to the nearest mineral, vacuums within its collector radius,
  returns when full or when its lifetime expires. Source: interactive reply.
- Q3 "What happens to the current `mysteryUfoScore` instant score burst?" —
  Answer (operator): **(A) Replace with minerals-only** — the UFO yields
  minerals only (transfer on return, or held-minerals + `2 × level` bonus on
  destruction); `mysteryUfoScore` is retired or repurposed. Source: interactive
  reply.
- Q4 "Per-level growth/caps for lifetime, capacity, radius, spawn interval?" —
  Answer (operator): **(A) Concrete defaults on the shared curve (k=0.3)** —
  lifetime 5→8 s, capacity 10→20, radius 20→40 px, spawn interval 30→12 s;
  destruction bonus `2 × level`; tunable in data. Source: interactive reply.
- Q5 "What destroys the drone?" — Answer (operator): **(A) Enemy bullets and
  enemy body-collision only** — player's own fire cannot destroy it. Source:
  interactive reply.
- Q6 "Gym parity home?" — Answer (operator): **(A) Extend `GymPowerUpsUtility`**
  (threat-free mineral field + `mystery_ufo` drops); destruction covered by
  shared-core tests. Source: interactive reply.

# Balance the levels of all enemy sounds

> **Headline:** Enemy SFX levels are wildly inconsistent (measured ~7.9× peak and ~9.3× RMS spread across the 26 enemy cue assets, with one near-clipping outlier), and their pitched content is not anchored to the battle-scenes' musical scale. This item rebalances every enemy cue onto category-relative amplitude tiers and snaps all pitched oscillator automation to A natural minor, using the ToneForge `tf analyze` tooling to measure and verify.

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug

## Problem statement

Some enemy SFX are significantly louder than others, which distorts the mix and makes enemy actions inconsistent to read by ear. Measured over the 26 committed enemy cue assets in `public/audio/sfx/`: peak amplitudes span **0.059 → 0.465 (~7.9×)** and RMS spans **0.014 → 0.128 (~9.3×)**; the Scout fire shot (`weapon-laser-zap.1.wav`, RMS 0.298, peak 0.977, near-clipping) is roughly 4× louder than every other enemy cue even after the existing 0.5× runtime scale. In addition, enemy cue pitches are arbitrary frequencies rather than notes of the battle-scenes' musical scale, so the SFX do not sit in the tonal world of the game.

## Users

- **Players** — need consistent, legible audio feedback: enemy fire, advance warnings, spawns and destruction booms should read at coherent relative loudness, with no cue jumping out of the mix or hurting the ears.
- **Producer / audio direction (Ross)** — needs enemy SFX to sit in the *selected battle-scenes scale* (provisionally **A natural minor**), uniform within tier, so the palette matches the game's musical identity.
- **Developers** — need measurable invariants (amplitude tiers + scale conformance) encoded in a guard test so the balance cannot silently regress on later recipe edits.

User stories:

- As a player, I want no enemy sound to blast louder than the rest, so I can track threats by ear without volume jumps.
- As a producer, I want every enemy cue's pitched content to land on a note of the battle-scenes scale, so the SFX feel part of the game's musical world.
- As a developer, I want the amplitude/scale invariants enforced by an automated check, so future recipe changes that break the balance fail the build.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Analysis report committed:** `tf analyze` is run over every committed enemy cue asset; a deterministic, documented report (peak, RMS, crest factor, spectral centroid, duration per cue; pre-change spread of ~7.9× peak / ~9.3× RMS called out) is committed (predicted `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md`), including the post-change values.
- [ ] **AC2 — Category-relative amplitude tiers:** every enemy cue asset sits within **±1.5 dB** of its documented category RMS target — Ambience `dive-loop` ≤ 0.02; Subtle one-shots (spawn, advance, light fires, dive-start, bullet-destruction) target 0.055; Heavy one-shots (destructions, tank-fire, boss-fire/hit/phase-cue/spawn, boss-phase-transition) target 0.090 — with every peak ≤ **0.50**, no clipping, and multi-seed variant ranges (enemy-destruction, diver-destruction) internally consistent (< 0.5 dB across variants).
- [ ] **AC3 — Scale conformance (A natural minor):** every pitched-oscillator automation point (start / end / waypoints) in every enemy recipe snaps to the nearest **A natural minor** note (`A B C D E F G`, equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz). Filtered-noise-only cues are documented as unpitched / conformant-by-nature. The multi-seed pitch-jitter ranges are re-derived as **scale-degree variants** (each seed starts on a different A-minor note and descends to an A-minor note), preserving per-kill variation without off-scale pitches.
- [ ] **AC4 — Scout fire resolved:** the scout fire shot (`playScoutFireSound`, currently the near-clipping existing-recipe asset `weapon-laser-zap.1.wav`) is brought into a target tier — recommended via a new in-repo baked recipe `aihell-scout-fire` preserving the "high square laser sweep" character — and the existing `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` (0.5×) runtime behaviour is unchanged (its tests still pass).
- [ ] **AC5 — Validation, docs, full suite:** a guard test asserts AC2 + AC3 over every enemy entry in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` (via the audio build/verify path, e.g. extended `build-audio` verification) and passes with the new assets (`npm run build-audio:verify`); all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes (recipe amplitude tiers + scale table in `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md`, README/guide references, code comments); the full project test suite and `npm run build` (including the audio render + checksum update) pass.

## Constraints

- **Never edit the `../ToneForge` sibling checkout** (repo rule, `audio/toneforge/README.md`). Any fix to the shared existing-recipe Scout fire asset must be a game-side in-repo recipe, not a ToneForge edit.
- **Deterministic pipeline:** recipes stay seed-reserved and data-only; `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` must be regenerated; reproducibility (render twice → byte-identical) must hold; `npm run build-audio:render` is the render path.
- **Runtime behaviour unchanged except through assets:** the audio pipeline (baked WAV via Phaser, master SFX gain, beat-accent scheduling, `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` 0.5, burn-time scale constants) is not rearchitected; balance changes are baked into recipes/assets (plus at most a cue-routing change for Scout fire).
- **Scale is provisional:** A natural minor is the agreed default for this item (operator-confirmed), pending the Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W); any reconciliation if that chapter documents a different battle scale is a small separate follow-up, not scope here.
- Game ↔ gyms parity: no gameplay behaviour changes are involved; any `effects.ts` touch must keep the shared path identical everywhere.
- UK English; Markdown; all project rules apply (tests via the test skill, commit hygiene, work-item association).

## Existing state

- The enemy cue set (26 assets) and their `tf analyze` metrics: spawn (enemy-spawn 0.068 RMS), destruction (enemy 0.098, diver 0.085, boss 0.128), advance (tank 0.091, scout/phaser 0.056), fire (tank 0.121, boss 0.104, diver 0.044, phaser 0.036, swarm-burst 0.038, scout = `weapon-laser-zap` 0.298/0.977 peak), dive (dive-start 0.069, dive-loop 0.014), boss (spawn 0.073, hit 0.095, phase-cue 0.098, phase-transition 0.069), bullet-destruction 0.067.
- All pitched automation values are currently arbitrary frequencies (e.g. enemy-spawn 220→880 Hz already in A minor; tank-fire 90→28 Hz, phaser-advance 660→880 Hz are off-scale).
- The `weapon-laser-zap.1.wav` Scout fire asset nearly clips (peak 0.977) and is the single worst offender.
- Music/scale terminology is not yet in the GDD (only "out of MVP scope" §7.3); the GDD Audio Design Chapter work item exists but is unimplemented.

## Desired change

- Analyse every enemy cue with `tf analyze` and commit the report.
- Edit the enemy recipes: retune per-node gain to the tier targets (verify with `tf analyze` on the rendered WAVs) and snap every pitched automation point to the nearest A natural minor note; convert jitter ranges to scale-degree variants; add a balanced in-repo `aihell-scout-fire` recipe and re-point `playScoutFireSound` at it.
- Re-render via `npm run build-audio:render` (updates WAVs + checksums), run the guard test and full suite, and update the docs.

**Key Files:**
- `audio/toneforge/recipes/*.yaml` — enemy recipes: gain-tier tuning + scale-note automation points (25 recipes; multi-seed variants enemy-destruction, diver-destruction, boss-phase-cue); new `aihell-scout-fire.yaml`
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — add `aihell-scout-fire` cue entry (and retire/swap `weapon-laser-zap` for `playScoutFireSound`) if AC4 option chosen
- `public/audio/sfx/` and `public/audio/sfx/checksums.json` — re-rendered enemy assets + digests
- `docs/AUDIO_ENEMY_BALANCE.md` (new) — `tf analyze` report, amplitude tier table, A-minor scale table, variant mappings
- `docs/AUDIO_TONEFORGE_CUE_MAPPING.md` — amplitude tier + scale-conformance columns for enemy cues
- `src/audio/effects.ts` (+ `src/audio/effects.test.ts`) — scout-fire asset routing change only
- guard test (new or extended, e.g. `scripts/build-audio.test.ts` / `src/audio/enemyBalance.test.ts`) — asserts AC2 + AC3 from `manifest.json` against committed WAVs
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §7.3 note that enemy cues are pitched to A natural minor (small)

## Related work

- **Update GDD with Audio Design Chapter (AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W)** — open; will document "Recommended Scales & Modes" — source of the future battle-scale reconciliation.
- **Switch game audio from procedural Web Audio to ToneForge (AH-0MUTUOB7X007PR9J)** — parent epic; this item is post-migration SFX palette work.
- **Reduce the volume of shots for Tank and Scout (AH-0MV74ROYR009X8U3)** — completed; established `TANK_SCOUT_FIRE_VOLUME_SCALE` 0.5 precedent for enemy-fire loudness.
- **Deterministic WAV build pipeline (AH-0MUTYV8FU007X7JD)** — completed; the render/verify/checksum machinery this item re-runs and extends.
- **Cue-to-recipe mapping and unused-cue audit (AH-0MUTYV7SQ005HURT)** — completed; authoritative cue catalogue updated here.
- **Update audio documentation (AH-0MUTYV9QV0000HDT)** — completed; documented the asset pipeline the docs updates touch.
- **Automate the balance-tuning loop (AH-0MV8Q5EYE001R715)** — in progress; gameplay tuning CLI, distinct scope (note as potential future home for the audio guard).
- **Improve thruster audio (AH-0MV01G4NL009JK92)** — completed; established the ≤ 0.2 player-cue ceiling the enemy tiers sit alongside.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Provisional scale (assumption):** A natural minor is the agreed default; if the Audio Design Chapter later specifies a different battle scale, the A-minor conformance needs re-snapping (small follow-up, tracked on AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W). Documented in the brief and the recipe catalogues.
- **Scout fire character drift (medium):** replacing `weapon-laser-zap` with an in-repo recipe preserves the "high square laser sweep" intent rather than the exact bytes; audition to confirm, and document intent in the recipe.
- **Jitter → scale-degree variants (medium):** the pitch-variation distribution changes from free ±15 % to discrete scale degrees; verify by audition that repeated kills still feel varied (three A-minor anchor notes per range keep variety).
- **Build cost (low-medium):** re-rendering the full enemy set takes minutes (`npm run build` already ~5 min, cf. AH-0MV87694J009Z34V); the auto-mode fingerprint forces the needed re-render once; verify path (`build-audio:verify`) is fast.
- **Scope creep:** player / weapon / power-up / victory/defeat cues have their own documented volume ceilings and are intentionally out of scope; any imbalance found in them later becomes a separate linked item.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What is 'the selected scale' for the battle scenes?" — Answer (operator): "(b) Default to A natural minor (Aeolian)". Source: interactive reply, 2nd round after repo search found no documented scale (GDD §7.3 still says music out of MVP scope; Audio Design Chapter AH-0MVAUUV1U005UM4W unimplemented). Prior answer attempt: none accepted — first round answered "check GDD/audio design doc; ask again if absent"; repo check confirmed absent, Q1 re-asked and answered (b). Adopted as the conformance scale (AC3).
- Q2: "Amplitude balancing policy ('reasonable spread')?" — Answer (operator): "(b) Category-relative targets". Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC2 (three tiers + ambience, ±1.5 dB window).
- Q3: "What counts as 'falling on a scale note' for frequency conformance?" — Answer (operator): "(a) Snap every pitched-oscillator automation point; noise-only cues conformant-by-nature". Source: interactive reply. Adopted as AC3.
- Issue-type decision: set to **bug** (corrects incorrect/inconsistent audio output); operator offered no objection when informed.

# Dev-mode telemetry upload to dev server with automatic evaluation

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** feature

## Problem statement

Recording a human play session for balance statistics (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) currently
requires the operator to discover and run the `npm run record` tool (which needs a
display + Playwright), or to manually dig a multi-megabyte string out of the player's
browser `localStorage` and paste it into a file (awkward, error-prone, size-limited).
There is no way to get telemetry from **any** browser hitting the dev server. We want a
dev-mode-only, zero-effort flow: the game itself collects the run, and at the end of
the game uploads the telemetry file to the server the game is running on; the server
stores it in `recordings/` and automatically runs the human evaluation on it.

None of this must be reachable when dev mode is not enabled (production builds, static
hosting, `vite preview`/`vite build` output).

## Users

- **As a maintainer**, I want any browser playing the dev-mode game to automatically
  deliver its recorded run telemetry to the dev server and have the human evaluation
  run on it, so I can collect balance statistics without any manual export step.
- **As a player/operator in dev mode**, I want telemetry collection to be controllable
  via a game setting (on by default), so I can opt out of upload without restarting the
  server.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Dev-only feature gate.** A fresh `npm run dev` game session (no special env vars)
   collected the run's telemetry by default and uploaded it at run end; the upload
   mechanism and the collection-on-by-default behaviour are unreachable in a
   production build. A dev-only enforcement test asserts no production call site /
   production bundle path can enable upload or collect-on-by-default.
2. **Setting (on by default).** A new game setting, e.g. "Share telemetry with the dev
   server (dev mode)" in `SettingsScene`, persisted in the existing settings store,
   defaults to **on**. When off, the dev game neither collects nor uploads telemetry.
   The setting is inert (ignored) in non-dev builds.
3. **Upload at end of game.** At run end (the existing `_finishRun`/run-end hook), and
   only when dev mode + setting on, the game POSTs the local JSONL sink's accumulated
   telemetry (`ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`) to the dev server the page was served from
   (same-origin fetch; no change to production telemetry/consent config). The upload
   is fire-and-forget and must not block or crash the game.
4. **Server-side receipt.** The dev server (Vite dev-only middleware, `apply: 'serve'`,
   mirroring `configCsvPlugin`) exposes an upload endpoint. On receipt it validates
   the body against the telemetry schema/recording reader, stores it in the
   `recordings/` folder using the existing `session-<timestamp>.jsonl` naming, and
   returns a confirmation. Malformed bodies are rejected (4xx) and never written.
5. **Automatic evaluation.** After a valid recording is stored, the human evaluation
   pipeline runs automatically on it (the existing `--human` path producing
   `human-balance-report.json` and companions under an `eval-output/`-style location).
   The evaluation runs asynchronously so it never blocks the game or the upload
   response; its completion/summary is logged. The full existing `npm run record` /
   `npm run evaluate -- --human` flows continue to work unchanged.
6. **Tests + docs.** Tests cover: the setting (default on, persistence, dev-only
   behaviour), the uploader (fires at run end with the sink content when dev+on,
   no-op otherwise), the server middleware (valid/invalid bodies, storage path, eval
   trigger, dev-only registration) and the dev-only enforcement scan. Docs
   (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`) describe the dev-mode
   auto-upload + automatic evaluation flow. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- **Dev-tooling only.** No production call site, no change to production
  telemetry/consent config (`VITE_TELEMETRY_CONSENT`, consent prompt). Production
  builds never collect or upload via this path.
- Reuse the existing telemetry framework sinks and record schema — no new recording
  mechanism, no schema divergence.
- The existing `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` local sink content is the canonical payload;
  the sink's localStorage content is left intact after upload (existing
  `npm run record` and inspection flows must keep working).
- No PII handling change: the payload is the same schema-only recording already
  written by the local dev sink.
- Same-origin upload (the page is served by the dev server), so no CORS work.
- Evaluation reuse: the shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline (and its
  `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` core) is invoked as-is rather than reimplemented.

## Existing state

- `src/telemetry/` — consent-gated framework; local dev sink writes JSONL to
  `localStorage` under `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`; disabled by default (`VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`).
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — typed `SettingsRecord` persisted under
  `ai_hell_settings` (volume, mute, bindings); settings scene reads/writes it.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_finishRun()` (≈3262) is the run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()` and emits the dev-gated run-ended signal.
- `vite.config.ts` + `vite/plugins/configCsvPlugin.ts` — the established dev-only
  middleware pattern (`apply: 'serve'`, Vite plugin with HTTP endpoints); a telemetry
  upload plugin should follow it.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — `parseRecording` /
  `parseTelemetryJsonl` for validating and splitting the flat record stream.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — the `--human` evaluation pipeline
  (same-seed comparison + `human-balance-report.json` from the shared helper,
  AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN).
- `recordings/` is gitignored (dev play recordings, AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ).

## Desired change

1. New `SettingsRecord` field (e.g. `shareTelemetryDev: boolean`, default `true`),
   surfaced as a toggle in `SettingsScene`; inert unless `import.meta.env.DEV`.
2. In dev mode, when the setting is on, the game enables the local jsonl sink (the
   default dev config currently requires `VITE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` — this feature
   makes a stock `npm run dev` collect when the setting is on) and, at `_finishRun()`,
   POSTs the sink's JSONL content to the dev server.
3. New dev-only Vite plugin (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`, registered
   `apply: 'serve'`) exposing e.g. `POST /api/telemetry/upload`: validate → write
   `recordings/session-<timestamp>.jsonl` → trigger the human evaluation asynchronously
   (spawn `node scripts/evaluate.mjs --human <file> --out <eval-output>/uploaded/<ts>` or
   invoke the CLI core via SSR) → log the result.
4. Dev-only enforcement test (mirroring the existing human-stats scan) asserting neither
   the upload path nor the on-by-default collection is reachable from production
   sources/builds.
5. Docs update (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md`).

## Key Files

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — new setting field + default.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` — dev-only toggle (place/naming to be confirmed at plan time).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — dev+setting gate at `_finishRun()`, uploader call.
- New uploader module (game-side, e.g. `src/telemetry/upload.ts` or
  `src/core/devTelemetryUpload.ts`) — dev-only, fetch + no-op otherwise, tested.
- `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` (+ `.test.ts`) — dev-only upload middleware +
  evaluation trigger.
- `vite.config.ts` — register the new dev-only plugin.
- `scripts/recording.mjs` / `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` — payload validation reuse.
- `scripts/evaluate.mjs` + `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` — automatic evaluation trigger.
- `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/recording-and-replay.md` — documentation.

## Related work

- **Collect balance statistics from human player games** (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN) — the
  human `BalanceReport` the automatic evaluation produces; upstream motivation.
- **Dev recording, analysis and replay/ghost tooling** (AH-0MUY08W7Y004GATZ) — the
  recording path (`npm run record`, `parseRecording`) and `recordings/` folder.
- **Telemetry framework** (AH-0MUY08VJ9006BHJO / AH-0MUY08VVQ007HSSH) — record schema,
  sinks, consent gates this feature builds on.
- **Periodically validate the human experience** (AH-0MV7WVHU0000U775) — downstream
  consumer of human balance statistics this flow feeds.
- **configCsvPlugin** (AH-0MTZWZ9TE009CVUA) — dev-only middleware pattern to mirror.
- **Human balance-statistics test suite** (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) — the test coverage the
  auto-evaluation flow should extend (found by automated related-work scan).
- **Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry** (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4) —
  completed production-telemetry precedent; related but **not** a duplicate of this
  dev-mode-only auto-upload flow (found by automated related-work scan).
- Full automated related-work report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-AH-0MVBHRLY8004BGDN.md`.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** dev-mode detection is `import.meta.env.DEV` (browser) and
  `apply: 'serve'` (server middleware); a production build/static host cannot reach
  the upload endpoint or on-by-default collection.
- **Assumption:** the payload is the local sink's accumulated JSONL and the sink is
  left intact after upload; repeated runs re-upload the whole accumulated stream
  (possible duplicate lines across sequential runs — mitigation: acceptable for dev
  data; a "capture window" or clear-after-upload can be negotiated at plan time).
- **Assumption:** uploads are validated with the existing recording reader
  (`parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics); only schema-valid records are stored.
- **Assumption:** automatic evaluation reuses the shipped `--human` pipeline
  (balance report + comparison artifacts) under a timestamped output directory; the
  exact trigger mechanism (child process vs in-process SSR) is an implementation
  decision assessed at plan time.
- **Risk:** enabling collection by default in stock `npm run dev` changes the
  telemetry gate's current "disabled unless env-flagged" default — must remain
  dev-mode-only, verifiable by the enforcement test and a production-build check.
- **Risk:** running Vite SSR evaluation inside the dev-server process could contend
  with the running server — prefer a spawned child process for the async evaluation.
- **Risk:** `npm run dev` currently opens a browser via `server.open` — unchanged;
  the uploader works from any browser (including a LAN/remote client) because the
  page and server are same-origin as served.
- **Scope guard (scope-creep risk):** enhancements such as a per-run "capture
  window", clear-after-upload, per-browser opt-out dashboards, or any
  production-facing variant are deliberately **out of scope** here; the first two
  are recorded as plan-time decisions and the rest would be new work items.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN** – Collect balance statistics from human player games (dev mode only) (completed)
- **AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7** – Human balance-statistics test suite (completed)
- **AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4** – Realistic demo/attract bot framework + playtester telemetry (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: acceptance, accumulated, already, api, apply (+296 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: accumulated, already, api, apply, asserting (+270 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: 0mtzwz9te009cvua, accumulated, already, api, apply (+258 more)


## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The seed context (operator-authored brief) was complete enough to draft directly;
no blocking clarifying questions were required. The entries below record the
decision points resolved from the repository/worklog rather than by interview.

- **Q: Is there an existing dev-only upload endpoint or uploader module to reuse?** —
  Answer (agent, repo search): No. `vite/plugins/` contains only `configCsvPlugin`;
  `src/telemetry/transport.ts` is the consent-gated framework transport, not a
  dev-server uploader. Conclusion: a new dev-only Vite plugin
  (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) + a game-side uploader module are
  required. Evidence: `vite/plugins/`, `src/telemetry/transport.ts`.
- **Q: Which run-end hook hosts the upload?** — Answer (agent, repo search):
  `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` `_finishRun()` (the existing run-end hook that already
  calls `runTelemetry.runEnd()`). Evidence: `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`.
- **Q: Reuse validation vs invent a parser?** — Answer (agent, repo search):
  Reuse `scripts/recording.mjs` `parseRecording` / `parseTelemetryJsonl` semantics.
  Evidence: `scripts/recording.mjs`, `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs`.
- **Q: Reuse the evaluation pipeline or reimplement?** — Answer (agent): Reuse the
  shipped `scripts/evaluate.mjs --human` pipeline / `src/ai/eval/cli.ts` as-is.
- **Q: Is this a duplicate of existing completed work?** — Answer (agent, worklog
  search): No. The automated scan surfaced (AH-0MV7WVEWL005XEMN),
  (AH-0MV8ISNNY003FHQ7) and (AH-0MUY089KR003F8S4), all related but addressing
  upstream/downstream or production-telemetry concerns; none provides the
  dev-mode-only auto-upload + auto-evaluation flow. Duplicate check performed — no
  overlapping completed item found.
- **Q: Exact trigger mechanism for the async evaluation (child process vs in-process
  SSR)?** — Answer (agent): **OPEN QUESTION (plan-time decision).** The brief's
  stated preference is a spawned child process to avoid contending with the running
  dev server; to be confirmed at plan time.
- **Q: Capture window / clear-after-upload semantics?** — Answer (agent): **OPEN
  QUESTION (plan-time decision).** Default in the brief is to leave the local sink
  intact and accept possible duplicate lines across sequential dev runs; a capture
  window or clear-after-upload is negotiable at plan time.

scaled copy of the player ship that seeks minerals, vacuums them within its
collector radius, returns home and pays out.

## Target outcome

`src/entities/MysteryUfoDrone.ts` is a self-contained neon-vector entity with
the full seek → collect → return → payout lifecycle, lifetime/capacity
termination, and the agreed destruction contract.

## Minimal implementation

- New `MysteryUfoDrone` entity following the `Harvester` seek pattern
  (`setSeekTargets` + nearest-live-mineral steering) and the code-drawn
  graphics convention (no external art).
- Constructor takes the resolved level values (lifetime, capacity, radius).
- State machine: SEEK → COLLECT (vacuum minerals whose centre enters the
  radius) → RETURN (when full or lifetime expires) → PAYOUT → gone.
- Expose read-only accessors for tests (state, held minerals, target).
- Destruction contract: `onEnemyBullet`/`onEnemyBody` mark it destroyed and
  expose held minerals for the drop; a player-bullet check is a no-op.
- Unit tests (`MysteryUfoDrone.test.ts`) for the lifecycle and destruction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Level-0 drone: lifetime 5 s, capacity 10 minerals, collector radius 20 px,
  all overridable from resolved level data.
- The drone actively seeks the nearest live mineral, collects minerals whose
  centre enters its collector radius, returns to the player and pays out
  when it has collected its capacity **or** its lifetime expires (whichever
  comes first), and disappears after payout — verified by unit tests
  asserting the seek → collect → return → pay out flow.
- Termination fires on either capacity reached **or** lifetime expiry,
  whichever comes first, and the drone disappears after payout with exactly
  the held minerals in the pay-in.
- An enemy bullet or enemy body collision destroys the drone and exposes its
  held minerals for the drop; the player's own fire cannot destroy it.
- The drone is rendered as a scaled-down player-ship entity, code-drawn
  neon-vector, no external art.

## Parent AC covered

Covers parent AC2 (seek/collect/return/payout flow, lifetime/capacity
termination, level-0 defaults) and the destruction behaviour of AC5.

# Intake Brief — Increase the number of waves in the levels, add mini-bosses

**Work item:** AH-0MVCC8XSS007P01Z (epic, high)
**Headline:** Grow the campaign to exactly 10 waves per level (100 waves over 10
levels), add a bespoke mini-boss as the 10th wave of every level, introduce 10
net-new alien archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon types spread
across the levels, and wrap it in a mini-boss reward loop (upgrade an owned
permanent weapon/power-up **or** unlock a new weapon type from a ~50%-locked
pool) plus a checkpoint save/resume at each mini-boss.

## Problem statement

The shipped campaign has only 2–4 waves per level (29 waves total across 10
levels) and a single final boss after Level 10 — there is no mid-level payoff,
no escalation hook within a level, and no way to resume a run. The operator
wants every level to feel substantial (10 waves), each level to end in a
bespoke mini-boss that grants a meaningful permanent reward, the campaign to
offer genuinely new content for the later levels, and the player to be able to
pick the run up again after closing the game instead of starting over.

## Users

- **Player** — "As a player, I want each of the 10 levels to take 10 waves and
  end in a mini-boss, so the campaign keeps escalating within every level."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want a mini-boss kill to let me choose between
  upgrading one of my permanent weapons/power-ups and unlocking a new weapon
  type, so my ship keeps growing in the direction I choose."
- **Player** — "As a player, I want the game to save my progress at every
  mini-boss so I can close the game and resume from the last checkpoint
  instead of starting a new game."
- **Designer/content author** — "As a designer, I want 10 new alien archetypes,
  5 new power-ups and 5 new weapons spread across the 10 levels — alongside
  the existing roster — so the later levels introduce genuinely new content
  while every previous level's enemies can still appear."
- **Engineer** — "As an engineer, I want the new behaviour (mini-bosses,
  rewards, unlocks) to run through the shared core and be mirrored in the gym
  scenes, so gym↔game parity holds without divergent copies."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **10 waves per level, mini-boss as the 10th wave** — Every level 1–10 has
   exactly 10 waves; the 10th wave of each level is that level's mini-boss
   encounter (9 regular waves + mini-boss). The final boss still triggers
   after Level 10. Wave counts and progression are data-driven
   (`src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` / `LEVELS`) and verified by tests.
2. **Net-new content for later levels** — At least 10 net-new alien
   archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon types are added beyond
   today's catalogue (17 enemies / 11 power-ups / 11 weapons → ≥27 / ≥16 / ≥16),
   spread across the levels as appropriate, each exercised in a gym scene
   (gym↔game parity).
3. **Mini-boss reward** — Defeating each mini-boss grants exactly ONE choice:
   upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by one level, **or** unlock a
   new weapon type from the locked pool. ~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue
   is locked at Level 1 and becomes available through these mini-boss rewards.
   The choice is applied through the existing permanent-level machinery and
   choice overlay (`MineralChoiceScene`, `powerups/choice`).
4. **Checkpoint save/resume** — A checkpoint (level, wave, lives, score,
   minerals, permanent upgrade levels, unlocked weapons) is auto-saved to
   `localStorage` at each mini-boss; the main menu offers Continue/resume from
   the last checkpoint in addition to New Game; starting a new game clears it.
5. **Quality & documentation** — The full project test suite passes with the
   changes; campaign invariants (difficulty non-decreasing, level variety,
   archetype reuse) continue to hold with 10-wave levels; all related
   documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
   `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
   and the README.

## Constraints

- **Mini-boss is the 10th wave** (not an 11th phase) — 9 regular waves plus the
  mini-boss as wave 10 of each level (producer Q2).
- **Content is net-new** — the 10 aliens / 5 power-ups / 5 weapons are beyond
  the current catalogue, not counted against it (producer Q1).
- **One reward choice per mini-boss** (upgrade an owned item OR unlock a new
  weapon type); ~50% of weapon/power-up catalogue locked at Level 1
  (producer Q3).
- **Gym↔game parity** — gameplay changes must be mirrored in the gym scenes
  via the shared core; no divergent copies (AGENTS.md).
- Persistence follows the existing `localStorage` convention
  (`ai_hell_*` keys alongside settings/leaderboard).
- No CHANGELOG.md edits (managed by the ship release pipeline).

## Risks, assumptions & failure modes

- **Scope creep (content volume)** — 10 wave rows × 10 levels plus 10 aliens + 5 power-ups + 5 weapons + 10 mini-boss designs is large. Mitigation: treat this as an epic decomposed under the plan skill; content is data-driven and additive, so per-item ACs can land incrementally. Record extra opportunities (e.g. more archetypes, boss-specific audio) as linked work items, not scope.
- **Difficulty-curve rebalancing** — widening levels to 10 waves each changes the non-decreasing difficulty curve and wave-gating invariants. Mitigation: extend `difficulty-curves.csv` monotonically and keep/re-run the campaign invariant tests (`campaignInvariants.test.ts`, `campaignBalanceAudit.test.ts`, `campaignRoster.test.ts`).
- **Balance** — 10-wave levels and mini-bosses lengthen runs; assumed acceptable (producer Q2), but difficulty tuning is expected during implementation. Assumption: wave-10 target difficulty sits above the level's regular waves but below the following level's opening.
- **Unlock pool definition** — "~50% of the weapon/power-up catalogue" needs a concrete locked set. Assumption: the locked set is defined in data at implementation time, biased toward newly added and later-level items, and includes enough early options that a Level-1 player still sees choice.
- **Checkpoint scope** — saves permanent levels/unlocks and run state. Risk: checkpoint/continue interacting with telemetry, run-seed reproduction and leaderboard scoring. Mitigation: checkpoint stores the run seed and permanent progression; leaderboard entries from resumed runs remain valid via the existing serialisation path.
- **Save-compatibility** — a checkpoint written by an earlier build must not crash a later build. Mitigation: defensive parsing with safe defaults (same pattern as the `Leaderboard` corrupt-JSON fallback).
- Assumption: "all previous level enemy types can appear in higher levels" already holds via the sequencer and remains a constraint on the expanded levels (existing archetype-reuse invariant is kept).

## Existing state

- Levels: 10 already exist (`MAX_LEVEL = 10`, `BOSS_LEVEL = 11`); campaign is
  currently **29 waves** total (L1=2, L2=3, L3=3, L4=3, L5=2, L6=4, L7=4,
  L8=3, L9=3, L10=2), driven by `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` +
  hand-authored `LEVELS` in `src/waves/Formations.ts`.
- Enemies: 17 archetypes ship today (scout, diver, tank, phaser, swarm,
  asteroid, harvester + classic-arcade march, capturer, ghost-chase/ambush/
  flank/wander, grunt, raider, lane-traffic, orbital-strike). Levels 6–10
  already showcase the classic-arcade roster (AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2).
- Power-ups: 11 (shield, bomb, speed_boost, phase_shift, teleport, extra_life,
  magnet, mineral_scoop, smart_bomb, force_field, mystery_ufo). Weapons: 11
  (cannon, spread, dual, rapid, wave_laser, ricochet, cluster, options, nova,
  mortar, arc).
- A permanent/temporary level split exists (`powerUpLevels.ts`,
  AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP): hold-full rewards raise the
  permanent level for the run. A reusable choice overlay exists
  (`MineralChoiceScene` + `powerups/choice`).
- No mini-boss concept, no weapon/power-up unlock gating, and no run
  checkpoint/save (only settings, leaderboard and rules persist).

## Desired change

- Extend the campaign data to 10 waves per level (per-level mini-boss as wave
  10), keeping hand-authored `fixed`/`dynamic` mixing where it adds value.
- Add a per-level mini-boss wave/phase: WaveManager recognises the 10th wave
  of each level as a mini-boss encounter; PlayScene spawns the mini-boss,
  handles its defeat, and only then advances to the next level.
- Add 10 net-new alien archetypes, 5 net-new power-ups and 5 net-new weapon
  types, spread across the 10 levels (data + entities + spawners + gyms).
- Add the mini-boss reward: on mini-boss defeat, launch the choice overlay for
  exactly one choice (upgrade owned permanent item OR unlock a weapon type from
  the ~50%-locked pool); apply through existing permanent-level machinery.
- Add checkpoint save/resume: save at each mini-boss to `localStorage`;
  expose Continue from the main menu; clear on New Game.

## Key Files

- `src/data/difficulty-curves.csv` — extend to 10 rows per level; mark the
  10th wave as the mini-boss wave.
- `src/waves/Formations.ts` — `LEVELS` skeleton + per-level mini-boss wave
  entries.
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — recognise mini-boss wave; boss-gating per level;
  progression to next level only on mini-boss defeat.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — spawn mini-boss at wave 10; launch reward choice;
  write checkpoints; resume path.
- `src/scenes/MenuScene.ts` — Continue/resume entry point.
- `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/entities/enemyFactory.ts` + new
  entity/spawner modules (`src/waves/`, `src/entities/`) — 10 net-new alien
  archetypes + 10 mini-boss designs.
- `src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/utils/weapons.ts` — 5 net-new power-ups /
  5 net-new weapon types (IDs, catalogue entries, level curves).
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — permanent-level application for the
  upgrade path; unlock state for the locked pool.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts`, `src/scenes/MineralChoiceScene.ts` — reuse the
  choice overlay for the mini-boss reward (already launcher-agnostic).
- New checkpoint store module (e.g. `src/core/checkpointStore.ts`) + keys
  alongside `ai_hell_settings` / `ai_hell_leaderboard`.
- `src/scenes/gym/` — parity gyms for new aliens, weapons, power-ups and a
  mini-boss gym (pattern: `GymBoss.ts`).
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`,
  `README.md` — update wave tables, enemy/power-up/weapon catalogues, save-data
  section.

## Related work

- AH-0MT7O8KCY0059RA5 / AH-0MT7QQGBU008V4R0 — Game Design Document (10-level
  campaign, boss, power-up catalogues; save-data design §6.6).
- AH-0MU72ZK3P006CH9G — WaveManager wave/level progression (extension point).
- AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2 — 5 new levels showcasing the classic-arcade roster
  (existing later-level content; the "net-new" bar is measured beyond it).
- AH-0MUX802450085VZZ / AH-0MUX9T7C7003CBQP — permanent/temporary power-up and
  weapon level split (reward machinery basis).
- AH-0MUBVGI62004ED9Q — hold-full choice scene (`MineralChoiceScene`),
  reusable for the mini-boss reward.
- AH-0MUZMTSQF0054WI8 — dedicated boss-hit SFX cue (pattern for mini-boss
  audio).
- find-related report appended to this work item's description.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "At least 10 new aliens, 5 new power-ups, 5 new weapon types for the
  later levels" — measured against the current catalogue or net-new beyond it?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "net new — spread them across levels as you
  feel appropriate". Source: interactive reply on the work item. Research:
  current catalogue is 17 enemies / 11 power-ups / 11 weapons (verified in
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`, `src/powerups/types.ts`,
  `src/utils/weapons.ts`); the classic-arcade roster (AH-0MV29SBAQ000HQR2) is
  existing content, not counted toward the net-new bar.
- Q2: Is the mini-boss the 10th wave or an encounter after 10 regular waves?
  One shared mini-boss scaled per level, or bespoke per-level designs?
  — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "10th wave, 10 designs". Source: interactive
  reply. Interpretation: mini-boss **is** wave 10 of each level (9 regular
  waves + mini-boss), and there are 10 bespoke mini-boss designs, one per
  level.
- Q3: Reward + save model (reconcile the two reward sentences and the
  checkpoint requirement) — Answer (producer, 2026-10-17): "as recommended".
  Source: interactive reply. Recommended model (accepted): each mini-boss
  defeat grants ONE choice — upgrade any 1 owned permanent weapon/power-up by
  one level, OR unlock a new weapon type from the locked pool; ~50% of the
  weapon/power-up catalogue locked at Level 1, unlocked via mini-boss rewards;
  checkpoint auto-saved at each mini-boss (level, lives, score, minerals,
  permanent upgrade levels, unlocked weapons) to `localStorage`, with Continue/
  resume on the main menu.

# ffmpeg compile driver and output validation

## Goal

Implement the ffmpeg-driven part of the pipeline (AC1, AC5, AC6 of the
parent): trim, reorder, join and mux source clips **deterministically via
ffmpeg** into the three deliverable types (promo, showreel, highlight clips)
at game-native 960×540 with the game's own SFX audio, and validate the outputs
(decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

**User story:** As the maintainer, one command (`npm run compile:promo`)
turns my captured footage into the promo package, and the script tells me
loudly and clearly when ffmpeg or footage is missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — ffmpeg invocation.** Trims each selected segment to its mapped in/out
  points, reorders, concatenates and muxes audio deterministically; sources are
  the WebM (VP9+Opus, or VP8 fallback) produced by `npm run capture`.
- **AC2 — Three deliverable types.** Produces (a) a single compiled promo WebM
  of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (> 2 min), (c) several short
  highlight clips — all WebM at the game's full native 960×540 resolution with
  the game's own SFX audio track.
- **AC3 — Output validation.** A validation step confirms each deliverable is
  decodable, has non-trivial non-black pixels, carries an audio track, and is
  at 960×540; validation failures are reported with actionable messages.
- **AC4 — Clear errors.** Missing ffmpeg or missing source footage yields a
  clear error with installation/runtime hints (ffmpeg install commands in
  `--help` and docs), not a stack trace.
- **AC5 — npm entry point.** `npm run compile:promo` drives the pipeline; the
  driver documents inputs, outputs and prerequisites via `--help`.
- **AC6 — Hermetic separation.** The ffmpeg-dependent path is isolated from
  the pure logic; the pure parts remain unit-tested without ffmpeg (see the
  sibling pure/test items). An optional integration smoke test is gated on
  ffmpeg presence and real or synthetic footage.

- **Covers parent AC5:** **AC5 — Reproducible, committed compile pipeline.** A committed editor script (e.g. `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` + an `npm run compile:promo` script) drives the compilation **deterministically via ffmpeg** (installed on the host, per producer decision): trim, reorder, join and mux the source clips without hand-editing. The script (`--help`) documents inputs/outputs and prerequisites, fails with clear errors when ffmpeg or source footage is missing, and its pure parts (manifest/selection logic) are unit-tested hermetically.
- **Covers parent AC6:** **AC6 — Testing/validation.** The pure selection/planning logic of the compile script has hermetic unit tests; the delivered video files are validated (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio track present, correct resolution) by a validation step in the pipeline.

## Key files

- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — ffmpeg driver + validation step
- `package.json` — `compile:promo` script entry
- `scripts/compile-promo.test.ts` — extend hermetic tests; integration gated on ffmpeg

## Implementation notes

- Prefer `ffmpeg` filter/`-ss`/`-to` trimming + concat demuxer (or a re-encode
  concat pass if the container requires it — see the capture doc's MP4/VP9+Opus
  note); choose the deterministic option and document it.
- Keep the deliverables under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree; never
  commit video files.

## Deliverables

- Committed ffmpeg driver + validation, `npm run compile:promo`, clear error
  handling.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the pure edit-plan/selection logic (C3) and the editorial config
  (C4); consumes the series + anchor format from capture-export (C1).

# Phasers spawn in a line then snap to a formation

## Problem statement

When a wave containing orbital Phasers spawns, each Phaser travels from the wave's wormhole to the **grid/line** slot produced by its formation offset (`baseX + col × spacingX`), then **snaps** onto its orbital ring position on the first formation tick. Because a Phaser's orbital phase is derived from `offset.col × (π/2)`, any group larger than four Phasers repeats phases every four members — so with a scaled group (the difficulty sequencer can produce `phaser × 12`) three Phasers stack at each of the four points and the group appears to contain only four entities. The wave is harder to read than intended and the arrival looks broken.

## Users

- **Primary — player:** "As a player I expect a group of Phasers to stream out of the wormhole and settle smoothly onto their final orbital positions, and I expect to see every Phaser in the group, so I can read the telegraphed radial pattern and plan my dodges."
- **Secondary — developer / gym user:** "As a developer I expect the same orbital geometry to drive both the spawn-transit destination and the per-frame orbit, so the gym and the game cannot diverge (gym↔game parity, AGENTS.md)."

## Acceptance Criteria

- **No line then snap** — For an orbital (`phaser`) wave group, every Phaser's wormhole-transit destination is its **live orbital slot**, not the grid/line slot. During the spawn window the Phaser interpolates from the wormhole to its orbital slot and, when the spawn window ends, `applyFormationPosition` places it on that same point with no visible position jump (post-spawn position delta ≤ 1 px).
- **Distinct, evenly distributed phases for any count** — For a group of `N` Phasers, all `N` orbital phases are distinct and evenly distributed across the full turn (`phase_i = i × 2π / N`, `i = 0…N−1`). For `N = 4` this reproduces the existing square (0°, 90°, 180°, 270°); for `N = 12` twelve distinct orbital slots are produced with no two Phasers coincident.
- **Single shared orbital geometry** — One shared pure helper computes the orbital slot and is consumed by both the entity's `applyFormationPosition` and the scene's transit-destination resolver. No duplicated orbital maths (the repo-wide duplicate-body guard passes).
- **Gym↔game parity** — The same behaviour runs in `PlayScene` and in every gym scene that spawns Phasers (`GymFodderEnemies`), verified by tests on both paths.
- **Spawn behaviour otherwise unchanged** — Transit timing is unchanged (completes inside the existing 3 s spawn-protection window), and the existing `isSpawning` gates still apply during transit (bullets pass through, no firing, no body collision, no mineral absorption). The single-live `WormholeController` lifecycle is unchanged.
- **Testing/validation** — New unit tests cover the pure orbital-geometry helper (phase distinctness for `N = 4`, `N = 5`, `N = 12`; slot positions), the Phaser entity's on-ring placement, and the scene-level transit destination (game and gym). A regression test asserts that a >4-member Phaser group produces no coincident slots.
- **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (§4.1 E4 Phaser, spawn/formation sections) and `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.1 note the count-based orbital phase distribution and the wormhole→orbital-slot transit.
- **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- Do not change the Phaser's firing pattern, tell/advance-cue behaviour, health, visuals, orbit radius (`PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS`), or orbit angular speed (`PHASER_ORBITAL_SPEED`).
- Do not change spawn timing or the 3 s spawn-protection window.
- Do not change other enemies' formation or spawn behaviour; the shared helper must keep a sensible default (4) so single-entity constructors and existing tests are unaffected.
- Gym↔game parity: shared behaviour lives once in the shared core/helpers and is consumed by both the game and the gyms (AGENTS.md).
- Keep the pure orbital-geometry helper free of Phaser runtime dependencies so it is unit-testable.

## Existing state

- `src/entities/Phaser.ts`
  - `_computeOrbitalPhase(offset)` returns `(offset.row × 10 + offset.col) × PHASER_ORBITAL_PHASE_SPACING`, with `PHASER_ORBITAL_PHASE_SPACING = π/2` — only four distinct phases, so counts > 4 collide.
  - `applyFormationPosition(baseX, baseY, dt, _spacingX, _spacingY)` treats the formation base as the orbit centre and places the body at `(centre + PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS·cos θ, centre + PHASER_ORBITAL_RADIUS·sin θ)` with `θ = phase + _localPhase × PHASER_ORBITAL_SPEED`. Spacing is intentionally ignored.
- `src/utils/formations.ts` — `buildOrbitalPhaseOffsets(count)` returns `{ row: 0, col: i }` for `i = 0…count−1` (a line when fed through `computeFormationPosition`). There is no shared orbital-slot helper.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_spawnEnemy(spawn, origin)` starts the wormhole transit with a destination resolver that computes `baseX + offset.col × spacingX`, `baseY + offset.row × spacingY`. For orbital offsets this is a horizontal line, hence the snap when `applyFormationPosition` takes over.
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `_spawnFormation(offsets)` uses the same grid destination resolver (`formationBaseX + offset.col × spacingX`, …), with the same snap.
- `src/vfx/wormholeSpawn.ts` — `SpawnState`/`updateSpawnAnimation` already support a live per-frame destination (`destFn`), so the fix can resolve the orbital slot every frame without new transit machinery.
