## Problem

The full suite (`npm test` / `/skill:test --type full`) takes 4.3-6.9 minutes
wall clock. Measured from four sanctioned cached runs in `.worklog/cache/`:

| Run | Wall clock | transform | setup | import | tests | environment |
|-----|-----------|-----------|-------|--------|-------|-------------|
| 262.33s | 262.33s | 138.39 | 17.05 | 962.12 | 957.89 | 547.48 |
| 290.72s | 290.72s | 140.61 | 23.58 | 1017.28 | 1022.41 | 621.64 |
| 389.61s | 389.61s | 166.61 | 60.33 | 1293.00 | 1234.28 | 746.14 |
| 415.43s | 415.43s | 174.88 | 53.90 | 1469.52 | 1288.82 | 921.41 |

(Phase figures are summed across parallel workers, so they exceed wall clock;
the ratios identify where the time goes.) 270 test files / 5975 tests.

## Root causes (measured)

1. **Phaser import/transform dominates.** 89 of 270 files boot a real
   `Phaser.Game`. Phaser is 118 MB in node_modules with an 8.8 MB non-minified
   ESM bundle that `server.deps.inline: ['phaser']` forces Vite to transform
   per worker. `import` + `environment` + `transform` is ~2.5x the `tests`
   phase. `isolate: true` (default) gives every file a fresh module graph and a
   fresh happy-dom, so Phaser is re-transformed/re-evaluated ~270 times.
2. **591 of 633 `bootScene()` call sites use the legacy real-time boot**, which
   does a literal `setTimeout(150)` per boot — ~88.6 s of pure wall-clock
   sleeping, and the source of the load-sensitive flakes already filed as
   AH-0MUYALJ9S0002XXZ and AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK. Only 42 call sites pass
   `deterministicBoot: true`.
3. **165 explicit `setTimeout` waits summing 37.8 s** (e.g.
   `GameOverScene.test.ts` ~11.4 s, `MenuScene.test.ts` ~9.4 s,
   `Game.test.ts` 3x200 ms ticks).
4. **Real subprocesses in `scripts/` tests**: `build-audio.test.ts` (20 spawn
   sites, real node + shell), `capture-gameplay.test.ts` (7),
   `audio-balance-guard.test.ts` (7), `compile-promo.test.ts` (ffmpeg),
   `recording-cli.test.ts`, `setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts`.
5. **Cross-agent host contention.** Load average ~13 on 16 cores with several
   agents running suites concurrently; each run spawns ~15 fork workers.
   Concurrent runs share the symlinked `node_modules`, and the Vite dep
   optimiser has left 98 `node_modules/.vite/deps_temp_*` dirs (~854 MB) —
   evidence of repeated re-optimisation/collision. Spread 262s -> 415s (~58%
   inflation) tracks load.
6. **Structural growth**: 92 -> 270 test files since 2026-09-26 (3x). Heavy
   files: `PlayScene.test.ts` (240 `it()`, full-game boot per test),
   `GymFormationScene.test.ts` (122), `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` (102
   tests / 50 boots).

## User story

As a developer or agent, I want the fast feedback loop to complete in well under
a minute, so that implementation iterations and the pre-`in_review` gate do not
dominate wall-clock time and do not flake under load.

## Proposed approach (to be planned)

- Invert the `bootScene` default to deterministic; delete the real-time 150 ms
  path (removes ~88 s of sleeps and the load-sensitive flakes).
- Reuse one booted game per file/describe instead of per test.
- Split the suite into two Vitest projects: `unit` (`environment: 'node'`, the
  181 non-Phaser files / 3137 tests) and `integration` (happy-dom + Phaser),
  so the fast loop is genuinely fast and the heavy suite is gated.
- Consider `isolate: false` / `pool: 'threads'` for the integration project and
  a pre-bundled Phaser dep so it is not re-transformed per worker.
- Replace remaining `setTimeout` polling with fake timers / `game.step`.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A documented, measured baseline of the current full-suite wall clock and
  per-phase breakdown exists on this item (satisfied by the table above).
- AC2: The `unit` project (non-Phaser tests) completes in <= 60 s on an idle
  16-core host, measured via `/skill:test --type unit`.
- AC3: The full suite completes in <= 50% of the current baseline (<= ~150 s on
  an idle host) with the same test count (no test deleted to hit the target).
- AC4: Zero `setTimeout`-based boot sleeps remain in `src/test/gameHarness.ts`;
  every boot is deterministic.
- AC5: The full suite passes, including under concurrent load, with no new
  flaky-test items filed.
- AC6: `/skill:test --type full` still populates the audit-accepted full-suite
  cache entry (the gate contract is unchanged).

## References

- Cache evidence: `.worklog/cache/*/{metadata,stdout}.json|txt`
- Related: AH-0MUYALJ9S0002XXZ (flaky PlayScene victory SHUTDOWN under load),
  AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK (flaky PlayScene wave-accounting), AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0
  (test-skill runner suite resolution)
